description: Test next-nearest positional unions after excluding the first scored-sensitive pair
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,793 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 21 prior macro-attempts and 314 prior micro-trials in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0078/micro-0292, which retained 1,793 parameters at 99.01%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0078/micro-0293, whose union of positional groups represented by coordinates 244 and 1 produced 1,792 parameters but scored 98.97% and was rolled back. Hypothesis: that failure reflects coordinate-specific sensitivity rather than a universal pairwise-difference floor, so excluding exactly (1,244) and ordering all remaining candidates by ascending current absolute group-value difference can identify a still-neutral union. This parameterization-preserving compression is more informative than the nearest untested alternative of changing tensor family immediately because it directly discriminates pair sensitivity from the measured 4.202e-4 distortion boundary. Each micro-trial adds exactly one eligible union; the official runner alone accepts or rolls back. Stop at the first scored discard or error, at the 20-micro-trial cap, or if no eligible pair remains. Compute budget: at most 20 checkpoint migrations and official verifications or 30 wall-clock minutes, whichever boundary occurs first.
summary: Evaluated the three next-minimum-difference positional unions after excluding attempt-0078's rejected (1,244) pair. micro-0001 and micro-0002 qualified and were retained, moving the frontier from 1,793 parameters at 99.01% to 1,791 parameters at 99.01%; micro-0003 proposed 1,790 parameters and scored 98.91%, so it was discarded and rolled back. There were 2 accepts, 1 scored discard, and 0 errors. Compute used checkpoint migration plus 3 official verifications, no fresh optimization, over 3m32s wall clock. Stop reason: the first scored failure closed this revised nearest-eligible path before the 20-trial/30-minute cap.
